abstract: This is the first case report describing brachiocephalic vein thrombosis without compression by a metastatic tumour during chemotherapy for testicular cancer. According to previous reports of testicular cancer patients with a major thrombus, anticoagulant therapy was required to resolve all cases. However, in the present case, a major thrombus in the brachiocephalic vein disappeared without anticoagulant therapy. This 42-year-old man was diagnosed with testicular seminoma and multiple metastases to the para-aortic lymph nodes. After 3 cycles of cisplatin, etoposide and bleomycin (PEB) therapy, a major thrombus in the right brachiocephalic vein was recognized on a computed tomography (CT) scan. Although no anticoagulant therapy was undertaken, the thrombus in the right brachiocephalic vein was no longer visible on CT after the fourth cycle of PEB therapy.
abstract_ja: これは化学療法中に、転移腫瘍による圧迫を伴わない腕頭静脈血栓症を記述した最初の症例報告である。精巣がん患者で大きな血栓を有する既報例では、いずれも抗凝固療法が解消に必要とされてきた。本症例は42歳男性で、精巣セミノーマと傍大動脈リンパ節への転移と診断された。シスプラチン、エトポシド、ブレオマイシン（PEB）療法3クール後、コンピュータ断層撮影（CT）で右腕頭静脈に大きな血栓が認められた。抗凝固療法は行わなかったが、PEB療法の第4クール後のCTでは右腕頭静脈の血栓は認められなくなった。
